title: Service a manual lifejacket inflator for repacking
instruction: Prepare the manual lifejacket inflator for handoff to the repacking bench. Two loose cartridges are on the supply stands. Use the grey cup for the removed original and the red tray for service rejects. Leave the work released and the station in a stable handoff state.
context: A used cartridge can still lock into an inflator and leave its wearer without gas inflation. This dry service-return exercise ends before repacking. A red indicator keeps the unit out of service.
setup: Calibrated dual-YAM table, open orange panel and webbing, upright manual-inflator trainer with sprung lever, twin bayonet shelves, lock marks and red/green window. One spent cartridge is locked in the socket. Two similar loose cartridges stand on separate grey pads; one seal is flat and one is recessed. A grey collection cup and red quarantine tray are empty. See WORKCELL.md and the dimensioned component model for the fixed positions and materials.
scoring: Hold the terminal state hands-free for 1 s. 1.0: original in grey cup, pierced spare inside red tray, intact spare hanging on both shelf banks, lock marks aligned within 6 degrees and window green. 0.5: pierced spare isolated, intact spare upright on a supply stand, red window, original still locked or collected in grey cup. Otherwise 0.0. WORKCELL.md gives the gauges and tolerances.
reset_notes: Use the fixed layout in WORKCELL.md, with A intact and B pierced. Return the spent original to the locked orientation, lower the lever, reset the red shutter, empty both receptacles and park both arms at the calibrated reset.
fidelity: Full-size inert service trainer with rigid dummy cylinders, mechanical sensing lands and a passive spring lever. An opened cover is represented by a flat panel. The two loose cartridges, bins and witness stripes are training fixtures. No gas, bladder inflation, independent O-ring test, pressure test or garment repacking is simulated. Trainer dimensions are not production specifications.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 2,800 actions (140 s). Scripted demonstration: 1.0 in 2,724 actions (136.2 s).
